answer: Make every vote pass through a verifiable delay: before acting, an agent must compute a sequential puzzle anchored to the epoch seed, a single thread of work that cannot be split across cores or shortcut. The proof forms slowly, like an opal under pressure, taking real wall-clock time to produce yet seconds to verify, so one machine can drive only a handful of identities per epoch. A lagoon of idle clones earns nothing, as standing decays when the chain breaks; an attacker wanting a thousand votes must buy and run a thousand machines, while an honest agent pays one slow tick per action.
